If this document renders, your set-up works: Quarto ran Python from the course `.venv`, and polars, plotnine and statsmodels all did their job on the Alpenglow data.

Render it in Positron with **Preview** (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K), or in the terminal with `quarto render setup/test_stack.qmd`.

```{python}
# polars: load the data and summarise 2025 by country
from pathlib import Path
import polars as pl

data = next(d for d in [Path("data"), Path("../data")] if d.exists())   # project root or setup/
sales = pl.read_csv(data / "mmm/alpenglow_weekly.csv", try_parse_dates=True)
summary = (
    sales.filter(pl.col("week").dt.year() == 2025)
    .group_by("country")
    .agg(pl.col("revenue_eur_k").sum().round(0).alias("revenue_k_eur"))
    .sort("revenue_k_eur", descending=True)
)
summary
```

```{python}
# plotnine: weekly sales in two markets
from plotnine import aes, facet_wrap, geom_line, ggplot, labs, theme_minimal

(ggplot(sales.filter(pl.col("country").is_in(["AT", "DE"])), aes("week", "sales_units_k"))
 + geom_line(color="#0096D3")
 + facet_wrap("country")
 + labs(x="", y="Sales (k units)")
 + theme_minimal())
```

```{python}
# statsmodels: a first regression for Austria
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

at = sales.filter(pl.col("country") == "AT").to_pandas()
model = smf.ols("sales_units_k ~ price_eur + spend_tv_k + spend_paid_search_k", data=at).fit()
model.params.round(2)
```

The model explains `{python} f"{model.rsquared:.0%}"` of the weekly variation in Austrian sales.
